title: Slices
explain: A slice is a flexible view over an array that grows with `append`. `len` is how many items it holds and `cap` is how many fit before Go must allocate a bigger array. Slicing with `s[1:3]` shares the same memory instead of copying it.
code:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	nums := []int{1, 2, 3}
	nums = append(nums, 4, 5)
	part := nums[1:3] // shares memory with nums
	part[0] = 99
	fmt.Println(nums, part, len(nums), cap(nums) >= 5)
	copyOf := append([]int(nil), nums...)
	copyOf[0] = -1
	fmt.Println(nums[0], copyOf[0])
}
exercise: Remove the middle element of a slice without leaving a gap, using `append`.
tip: Always assign the result of `append` back, as in `s = append(s, x)`. It may return a new slice.
